relearning.title: Read: bacteria, helpful and harmful
relearning.description: A short reading with the studio-apartment analogy, worked examples and quick checks.

body.text:
**I can understand the different types of bacteria and the beneficial and harmful roles bacteria play in the environment and in human health.**

**Think of a studio apartment.** Everything is in one open room with no inside walls. A eukaryotic cell is more like a house with separate rooms (a nucleus and other organelles). Bacteria are the studio apartment: they are **prokaryotes**, so they have **no nucleus** and **no membrane-bound organelles**.

**What bacteria do have:** a **cell wall** on the outside, a **cell membrane** just inside it, **cytoplasm**, **ribosomes** to make proteins, and one circular chromosome of DNA in the **nucleoid** region. Some have **flagella** (whip-like tails) to move and **pili** (short hairs) to stick to surfaces.

**Two kingdoms:**
- **Eubacteria** ("true bacteria") are the most common. They live almost everywhere: soil, water, your skin and your gut. Bacteria are **ubiquitous** (found everywhere).
- **Archaebacteria** ("ancient bacteria") live in extreme places like hot springs, very salty lakes and vents on the ocean floor. They may be some of the oldest life on Earth.

**Three basic shapes:** **cocci** (spheres), **bacilli** (rods) and **spirilla** (spirals).

**Reproduction:** bacteria copy their DNA and split in two, which is called **binary fission**.

**Worked example:** A single cell is found in a boiling hot spring in Yellowstone. It has no nucleus. No nucleus means a prokaryote, and the extreme home points to **Archaebacteria**.

checks.prompt: A bacterium shaped like a rod is called a –
checks.explanation: Bacilli are rods, cocci are spheres and spirilla are spirals. Mixing up coccus and bacillus is the common mistake.

checks.prompt: Which structure do bacteria NOT have?
checks.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes, so their DNA floats in the nucleoid region with no nucleus around it. They do have ribosomes and a cell wall.

sections.title: Helpful and harmful roles

body.text:
**Most bacteria are helpful or harmless.** Only a small number cause disease.

**Helpful in the environment:**
- **Decomposers** break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.
- **Nitrogen-fixing bacteria** in soil and in the roots of plants like beans and clover turn nitrogen gas into a form plants can use.
- **Cyanobacteria** have chlorophyll and make their own food by photosynthesis, giving off oxygen.
- Some bacteria are used to clean up oil spills.

**Helpful to people:**
- **Normal flora** are the bacteria that always live in your gut and on your skin. Gut bacteria like *E. coli* help digest food and make vitamin K.
- Bacteria turn milk into **yogurt and cheese**, and cabbage into sauerkraut.
- Engineered bacteria make medicines such as insulin.

**Harmful:** bacteria that cause disease are called **pathogens**. Examples: strep throat (*Streptococcus*), food poisoning (*Salmonella*), tuberculosis, and Lyme disease, which ticks spread here in Wisconsin.

**Worked example 2:** A cell found in yogurt is rod-shaped and has no nucleus. It is a **bacillus** in Kingdom **Eubacteria**, and it is **helpful**: it ferments the sugar in milk to make yogurt.

**Antibiotics** kill bacteria, but they do nothing to viruses, so they do not cure a cold or the flu. Using them when they aren't needed, or not finishing them, helps **antibiotic-resistant** bacteria survive and spread.

**Watch out for:** thinking all bacteria are germs, mixing up Eubacteria (common, everywhere) and Archaebacteria (ancient, extreme), thinking bacteria have a nucleus, and thinking antibiotics work on viruses.

checks.prompt: Which is a helpful role bacteria play in the environment?

options.text: Turning nitrogen gas into a form plants can use

checks.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria feed plants and the whole food chain. Strep throat and Lyme disease are caused by pathogens, which are the small harmful group.

checks.prompt: Why won't an antibiotic cure a cold?

options.text: A cold is caused by a virus, and antibiotics only kill bacteria
Cold bacteria are too small for antibiotics to reach

checks.explanation: Colds and the flu are caused by viruses, and antibiotics only work on bacteria. Taking them anyway helps antibiotic-resistant bacteria spread.

relearning.title: Do: flip the bacteria cards, then classify a mystery cell
relearning.description: Flashcards with a 3-question self-quiz, then a mystery bacterium classified one step at a time.

cards.back: A cell with no nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles. All bacteria are prokaryotes.
"True bacteria": the most common kind, found almost everywhere (soil, water, skin, gut).
"Ancient bacteria" that live in extreme places like hot springs, salt lakes and ocean-floor vents.
How bacteria reproduce: copy the DNA, then split into two identical cells.

checks.prompt: Which kingdom of bacteria lives in extreme places like hot springs?
checks.explanation: Archaebacteria ("ancient bacteria") live in extreme places. Eubacteria are the common bacteria found almost everywhere.

checks.prompt: A sphere-shaped bacterium is called a –
checks.explanation: Coccus means sphere. A bacillus is a rod and a spirillum is a spiral.

checks.prompt: Bacteria reproduce by splitting into two identical cells. Type the name of this process.
checks.explanation: It is binary fission ("splitting in two"). Mitosis is the common wrong answer: bacteria have no nucleus, so they do not do mitosis.

sections.title: Worked problem: classify a mystery bacterium

body.problem: A single cell is taken from a cup of yogurt. Under the microscope it is rod-shaped and has no nucleus. Classify it and decide whether it is helpful or harmful.

steps.text: Is there a nucleus? No, so the cell is a prokaryote: a bacterium.
Where does it live? Yogurt is an ordinary place, not an extreme one like a hot spring, so it belongs to Kingdom Eubacteria.
What shape is it? A rod, so it is a bacillus. (Its name, *Lactobacillus*, even has "bacillus" in it.)
Helpful or harmful? It ferments the sugar in milk to make yogurt, so it is helpful.

checks.prompt: Your turn: a cell with no nucleus is found in water that is 90 °C, near a hot spring. Which kingdom is it in?
checks.explanation: No nucleus makes it a prokaryote, and an extreme home like a hot spring points to Archaebacteria. Fungi have a nucleus.

checks.prompt: *Streptococcus* causes strep throat. Using its name, what shape is it, and is it helpful or harmful?
checks.explanation: The name ends in -coccus, so it is a sphere. It causes a disease, so it is a harmful pathogen.

checks.prompt: Bacteria are prokaryotes. What does that mean?

options.text: They are made of many cells
They have no nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles

checks.explanation: A prokaryote is like a studio apartment: one open room with no nucleus. Bacteria still have a cell wall, ribosomes and DNA.

checks.prompt: Which statement about bacteria is true?

options.text: Most bacteria are helpful or harmless
All bacteria are germs that cause disease
Bacteria are only found in dirty places

checks.explanation: Only a small number of bacteria cause disease. Thinking all bacteria are germs is the common mistake.

sections.title: Old & Odd: Archaea, Bacteria & Protists - CrashCourse Biology #35

options.text: "Ancient bacteria" that live only in extreme places
"True bacteria": the most common kind, found almost everywhere

checks.explanation: Eubacteria are the common bacteria in soil, water, your skin and your gut. The ancient bacteria of extreme places are Archaebacteria, and no bacteria have a nucleus.

checks.prompt: Bacteria that cause disease are called –
checks.explanation: Pathogens cause diseases like strep throat and Lyme disease. Normal flora are the bacteria that always live in your gut and on your skin.

sections.shortAnswer: Explain one way Eubacteria and Archaebacteria are alike and one way they are different.
